and-or-not.label: And, Or, and Not
and-or-not.summary: Combine boolean conditions with `and`, `or`, and `not`, then use parentheses to make multi-part rules easier to read.

sc_and_true.title: When does and become true?
sc_and_true.prompt: Which statement about `A and B` is correct?
sc_and_true.hint: `and` requires every joined requirement to be true.

help.concept: `A and B` is true only when both `A` and `B` are true.
help.hint_1: If either side is false, the whole `and` expression is false.
help.hint_2: Choose the option requiring both sides.

options.a: It is true only when both A and B are true.
options.b: It is true when either A or B is true.
options.c: It is always the opposite of A.
options.d: It is true whenever A is false.

sc_not_flip.title: Reverse a boolean with not
sc_not_flip.prompt: If `logged_in = False`, what does `not logged_in` evaluate to?

help.hint_1: Start with the value stored in `logged_in`.

mc_or_cases.title: Choose the true or expressions
mc_or_cases.prompt: Which expressions evaluate to `True`? Choose all correct answers.
mc_or_cases.hint: `or` is true when at least one side is true.

help.concept: `or` fails only when both sides are false.
help.hint_1: Evaluate the left and right sides separately.
help.hint_2: Then ask whether at least one side is true.

mc_valid_age_and_name.title: Conditions that require both rules
mc_valid_age_and_name.prompt: A user is accepted only when `age` is at least 18 and `name` is not empty. Which conditions correctly enforce both requirements? Choose all that apply.
mc_valid_age_and_name.hint: Both the age rule and the non-empty-name rule must be required.

help.concept: Equivalent expressions are valid only if they still require both parts of the rule.
help.hint_2: `not (age < 18)` is another way to express age 18 or older.

dr_build_and_condition.title: Build an and expression
dr_build_and_condition.prompt: Put the tokens in order to check whether `score` is at least 50 and `passed` is true.
dr_build_and_condition.hint: Complete the comparison first, then join the boolean variable with `and`.

help.concept: A combined condition can join a comparison and an existing boolean value.

dr_if_elif_else_logic.title: Build a grouped boolean rule
dr_if_elif_else_logic.prompt: Arrange the tokens to express: weekend or holiday, and not raining.
dr_if_elif_else_logic.hint: Group the two free-day alternatives before joining the rain requirement.

help.concept: Parentheses can make the intended grouping of `or`, `and`, and `not` explicit.

fb_not_condition.title: Complete a not check
fb_not_condition.prompt: Choose the missing word to make the condition true when `ready` is false.
fb_not_condition.hint: Use the operator that reverses the value of `ready`.

help.concept: `not ready` is true exactly when `ready` is false.
help.hint_1: `and` and `or` combine values instead of reversing one.

fb_or_operator.title: Complete an either-or rule
fb_or_operator.prompt: Choose the operator that makes the condition true when either comparison is true.
fb_or_operator.hint: Either extreme temperature should make the condition true.

help.concept: `or` joins alternative conditions when either one is enough.
help.hint_1: `temp < 0` and `temp > 30` cannot both be true at once.
help.hint_2: Choose the operator that accepts either condition.

code_ticket_check.prompt: Read an integer age and then `yes` or `no` for whether the person has an ID. Print `allowed` only when age is at least 18 and the ID answer is `yes`; otherwise print `denied`.
code_ticket_check.hint: Join the age comparison and ID comparison with `and`.

code_free_day.title: Accept either free-day condition
code_free_day.prompt: Read `yes` or `no` for `is_weekend`, then `yes` or `no` for `is_holiday`. Print `rest` when either answer is `yes`; otherwise print `work`.
code_free_day.hint: Convert both answers to booleans, then join them with `or`.

code_not_logged_in.hint: Convert the answer to a boolean, then use `not logged_in`.

code_score_certificate.prompt: Read an integer score and then `yes` or `no` for whether the work is late. Print `certificate` when the score is at least 80 and the work is not late; otherwise print `no certificate`.
code_score_certificate.hint: Require the score threshold and `not late` together.

sketch_and_basics.title: Use and when every requirement must pass
sketch_and_basics.bodyMarkdown:
Use `and` when **both** sides of a rule must be true.

```python
age = 20
has_id = True

if age >= 18 and has_id:
    print("allowed")
else:
    print("denied")
```

The combined condition has two parts:

```python
age >= 18
has_id
```

`and` joins them.

The result is true only when both parts are true:

- `True and True` → `True`
- `True and False` → `False`
- `False and True` → `False`
- `False and False` → `False`

For an entry rule, being old enough is not sufficient by itself, and having an ID is not sufficient by itself. Both requirements must pass.

sketch_or_not.title: Use or for alternatives and not to reverse
sketch_or_not.bodyMarkdown:
Use `or` when at least one condition is enough.

```python
is_weekend = False
is_holiday = True

if is_weekend or is_holiday:
    print("rest")
else:
    print("work")
```

Because one side is true, the combined condition is true.

For two boolean values:

- `False or False` → `False`
- every other combination → `True`

Use `not` to reverse one boolean value:

```python
logged_in = False

if not logged_in:
    print("please sign in")
```

`logged_in` is `False`, so `not logged_in` becomes `True`.

Useful pairs to remember:

```text
not True  -> False
not False -> True
```

sketch_combining_clear_rules.title: Group a multi-part rule clearly
sketch_combining_clear_rules.bodyMarkdown:
A real rule can combine more than one boolean operator.

Suppose a learner may study outside only when it is a weekend or holiday **and** it is not raining:

```python
is_weekend = True
is_holiday = False
is_raining = False

if (is_weekend or is_holiday) and not is_raining:
    print("study outside")
else:
    print("study inside")
```

Read the rule in pieces:

1. `(is_weekend or is_holiday)` asks whether either free-day condition is true;
2. `not is_raining` requires rain to be false;
3. `and` requires both larger requirements to pass.

Parentheses make the intended grouping visible to the reader.

A good habit is to translate the Python back into plain language:

> weekend or holiday, and not raining

If the code no longer matches the rule you meant to write, simplify or regroup it before adding more conditions.
